text_content: dost-phivolcs kicked off the 5-day training on mainstreaming disaster risk reduction into local development, contingency planning, and emergency preparedness through the use of redas software for the provinces of dinagat islands and surigao del norte. the training is being held at southville hotel and convention center, butuan city on september 15, 2025. the program features three modules, including the use of redas for near-real time monitoring of earthquakes, tsunami and rain, for calculation of impacts, and for development of a communitys exposure database. mr. rosario jra. r. alon of dinagat islands pdrrmo and mr. cicero cosme p. tripoli, head of surigao del norte pdrrmo, delivered the opening remarks. dost-phivolcs director teresito c. bacolcol welcomed the participants and highlighted the importance of redas training in empowering the local government amidst disasters and climate change. ms. divina gracia b. bandola, programme associate of the world food programme, also sent her message of support to this initiative. participants from the province of dinagat islands include representatives from the pdrrmo, provincial planning and development office (ppdo), provincial engineering office (peo), provincial architects office (pao), provincial environment and natural resources office (penro), and the municipalities of basilisa, san jose, tubajon, cagdianao, libjo, dinagat, and loreto. meanwhile, participants from surigao del norte include representatives from the pdrrmo, ppdo, peo, sangguniang panlalawigan, and the municipality of san isidro. personnel from dpwh-province of dinagat islands, dost-caraga, dilg-caraga, depdev-caraga, ocd-caraga, caraga state university, world food programme, as well as guest participants from butuan ito na ang ika-54 na site sa buong bansa at ikalawa sa davao de oro na pagtatatagan ng early warning system for landslides (ews-l) sa ilalim ng dynaslope project. noong august 1113, 2025, isinagawa ang pre-implementation site assessment (pisa) bilang unang hakbang sa pagtatatag ng ews-l. layunin nitong buuhin ang pagkakaisa ng mga stakeholder upang epektibong aksyunan ang panganib ng landslide sa sitio candinuyan. mga naging aktibidad: detailed landslide hazard survey & global system for mobile communications (gsm) signal survey pagmamapa ng landslide area rapid needs and capacities assessment pakikipagkwentuhan at konsultasyon sa mga residente community orientation pormal na pagpapakilala ng ews-l sa komunidad nagkaroon din ng courtesy call sa lgu mabini at sa pamunuan ng brgy. golden valley, kung saan ipinahayag ng mga opisyal ang buong suporta sa proyektong ito. abangan ang mga susunod na hakbang tungo sa kinabukasang #ligtassalandslide sa sitio candinuyan! mayon volcano advisory 06 september 2025 5:30 pm this is a notice of increased seismic activity in mayon volcano. since 12:00 am today, 6 september 2025, a total of 26 volcanic earthquakes have been recorded by the mayon volcano network. these events registered at strengths of ml0.4-ml2.7 and most originated at depths of 5-10 kilometers beneath the northeast flank of the mayon edifice. mayon has been exhibiting non-uniform inflation or swelling in its northeastern sector since october 2024 and its south to southwestern sectors since march 2025 based on continuous gps, electronic tilt and edm ground deformation data. sulfur dioxide so2 emissions have remained near background levels, averaging 430 tonnes/day this year with the latest measurements on 3 september 2025 averaging 609 tonnes/day. increased seismicity today as well as longer-term swelling of the edifice could indicate that deep magma intrusion may be taking place beneath the volcano, which could increase the chances of steam-driven or phreatic eruptions occurring at the crater. dost-phivolcs would like to remind the public that mayon volcano is at alert level 1, which means that it is at an abnormal condition. although this means that no magmatic eruption is imminent as of present, the public is strongly advised to refrain from entering the 6-kilometer radius permanent danger zone (pdz) due to life-threatening hazards such as rockfall, landslides/avalanches, ballistic projectiles and short pyroclastic density currents (pdcs) or uson that could be generated by a sudden phreatic eruption from the summit. active stream/river channels and those identified as perennially lahar-prone areas on all sectors of the volcano should also be avoided especially during extreme weather conditions when there is heavy and prolonged rainfall. civil aviation authorities must advise pilots to avoid flying close to the volcanos summit as airborne ash and ballistic fragments from sudden explosions and pdcs may pose hazards to aircraft. dost-phivolcs maintains close monitoring of mayon volcano and any new development will be communicated to all concerned stakeholders. dost-phivolcs mayon volcano rescue group mourns loss of foster dog tiktok a local rescue group is mourning the loss of tiktok, a dog who died in a tragic accident after slipping out while in foster care and being hit by a car. tiktok had been fostered to protect her from a distemper outbreak at the shelter. rescuers said she was surrounded with love, but fate took a heartbreaking turn. once a victim of cruelty, tiktok was previously shot five times with improvised arrows in murcia, negros occidental. she was rescued by bach project ph on february 24, 2025, and made a full recovery. a short viewing will be held on september 8, from 10 to 11 a.m. at green meadows pet aftercare in negros, before her cremation. attendance will be limited. the group asks for understanding during this painful time and invites everyone to remember tiktok with love and prayers. bach project ph #allyouneedtoknow rescue group mourns loss of foster dog tiktok a local rescue group is mourning the loss of tiktok, a dog who died in a tragic accident after slipping out while in foster care and being hit by a car. tiktok had been fostered to protect her from a distemper outbreak at the shelter. rescuers said she was surrounded with love, but fate took a heartbreaking turn. once a victim of cruelty, tiktok was previously shot five times with improvised arrows in murcia, negros occidental. she was rescued by bach project ph on february 24, 2025, and made a full recovery. a short viewing will be held on september 8, from 10 to 11 a.m. at green meadows pet aftercare in negros, before her cremation. attendance will be limited. the group asks for understanding during this painful time and invites everyone to remember tiktok with love and prayers. bach project ph #allyouneedtoknow

may your paws find peace on the road to heaven, tiktok! tiktok, the brave aspin who was rescued in negros occidental and was recently celebrated after finishing her fun run last august 2025, has died in a tragic accident while in foster care. her sudden passing has left a heartbreak in the community that followed her journey from survival to recovery. in a facebook post, bach project said that tiktok "slipped out, ran, and was hit by a car." they explained that she was placed in foster care as their shelter continues to battle a distemper outbreak, and they wanted to ensure her safety and well-being. "as rescuers, we carry so much guilt when tragedies like this happen, even when we know we did our best. she was supposed to be safe. she was supposed to have more time. the what ifs are endless, and the pain of losing her is unbearable," they added. bach project ph is asking for understanding from the community during this painful time and invites everyone to join them in remembering tiktok's journey. building resilience together: dost-pagasa, bpsu signs moa for the bataan abucay doppler radar station 08 september 2025 | the dost-pagasa and bataan peninsula state university (bpsu) formalizes partnership for the establishment of the bataan abucay doppler radar station through a memorandum of agreement (moa) signing held at the amihan conference room, pagasa central office, quezon city. with the funding support from the office of the president, through the office of civil defense (ocd)/national disaster risk reduction and management council (ndrrmc), the bataan abucay doppler radar station will significantly enhance accuracy of weather forecasts through real-time data enabling local governments to issue timely warnings to communities, and plan disaster responses effectively. dost-pagasa administrator dr. nathaniel t. servando welcomed bpsu officials led by university president dr. ruby santos-matibag, campus director dr. walter valdez, and dean of instruction dr. dharell siano. through this significant agreement between our institutions, we not only strenghten our shared commitment to nation-building but also foster collaboration in research, innovation, and capacity-building, dost-pagasa administrator nathaniel t. servando said. dr. servandos appreciation is also extended to the ocd for closely collaborating with dost-pagasa in ensuring that lives and welfare of the filipino people are safeguarded during natural disasters. dr. marcelino q. villafuerte ii, deputy administrator for r&d, also expressed his gratitude to the bpsu for the establishment of the synoptic station in abucay, bataan in 2021, with this signing ceremony, our partnership begins again and we hope that it could futher enhance our collaboration, as we establish our radar station, for students to potentially use our datasets. bpsu president dr. santos-matibag highlighted that the signing ceremony is more than just a formal partnership, but a celebration of shared commitment to scientific process and public safety of all filipinos. she also said that bataenos are used to warnings pertaining to weather hazards, and this agreement highlights the universitys dedication to supporting research and innovation that address community needs, especially in drr. national capital region-pagasa regional services division (ncr-prsd) chief engr. lorenzo a. moron thanked bpsu president dr. santos-matibag and all involve, emphasizing that the ceremony today is more than technological advancement, but it also represents our promise to be better stewards of public safety. other dost-pagasa executive staff members in attendance were engr. juanito galang (chief of weather division), ms. thelma cinco (chief of climatology and agrometeorology division), mr. michael bala (oic of research & development and training division), and mr. oskar cruz (oic of hydrometeorology division). the pagasa-bpsu doppler radar station is expected to become a vital tool in strengthening the philippines disaster preparedness, providing more accurate forecasts and timely warnings for the protection of communities across the nation. #onedost4u text_content: spmc and bfp 11 sign moa, joining forces for safer communities the southern philippines medical center (spmc) and the bureau of fire protection region xi (bfp 11), headed by fcsupt junito f maslang, dsc, have officially sealed a partnership to strengthen emergency preparedness and ensure the health and safety of first responders. through a memorandum of agreement signed on 15 september 2025, both institutions committed to work hand in hand in addressing hazardous materials (hazmat), cbrne events (chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and explosive), and other medical contingencies that threaten public safety. under the agreement, spmc guarantees priority medical care for firefighters and bfp 11 personnel injured or taken ill in the line of duty. both parties will also engage in joint training exercises and knowledge-sharing programs to boost readiness and enhance response efficiency. in addition, a second memorandum of agreement provides that officers and personnel of bfp region xi may avail of emergency, medical, and hospitalization services at spmc which will be free of charge. these include burn treatments, minor surgical operations, post-admission treatments, and follow-up check-ups. the ceremony was graced by leaders from both sides, underscoring the importance of this milestone collaboration. representing bfp 11 were regional director fcsupt junito f maslang, assistant regional director for operations fssupt franklin o ratunil, mindanao team lead fssupt randolf v arbutante, and davao city fire district fire marshal fsupt donald r concepcion, along with other key officers. representing spmc were legal officer atty. karen bianca angeli s. cezar, medical center chief ii ricardo b. audan, md, and dr. fitzgerald c. arancel. this partnership stands as a testament to unity and preparedness, ensuring that our firefighters and first responders receive the care they deserve while safeguarding the greater community. text_content: disaster response update | ocd x conducts site inspection and provides assistance in flood-hit valencia city september 19, 2025 - the office of civil defense region x (ocd x) conducted a site inspection in valencia city, bukidnon after a flash flood on september 17, 2025 that affected more than 2,000 families. ocd x regional director and northern mindanao regional disaster risk reduction and management council (normin rdrrmc) chairperson antonio b. sugarol led the team in coordinating response operations and met with mayor amie g. galario and city drrm officer june ray a. valero to assess urgent needs. at the request of the valencia city lgu, ocd x facilitated the augmentation of three (3) water search and rescue (wasar) teams consisting of special operations group of the philippine coast guard, northern mindanao, the cagayan de oro city drrmd (cdo-cdrrmd) wasar team and 4id, pa wasar team. in coordination with the tactical operations group 10, philippine air force, two (2) black hawk helicopters airlifted the team from 4id, pa. these teams will augment and assist in the ongoing search and retrieval operations as four (4) persons still remain missing. read more: source: civil defense northern mindanao - at the foot of mayon volcano, teachers and division personnel of the department of education (deped) ligao city convened for a training on disaster readiness and risk reduction for volcano, earthquake, and tsunami hazards on september 25-27, 2025 at ligao city, albay. the event is co-organized by deped ligao city and dost-phivolcs. dr. nympha d. guemo, schools division superintendent of deped ligao city welcomed the participants of the activity while dr. ma. mylene m. villegas, deputy director of dost-phivolcs, delivered her message of support. experts from dost-phivolcs led a series of lecture discussions related to volcano, earthquake, and tsunami hazards and their mitigation measures. dr. villegas discussed volcanoes and volcanic hazards. ms. charmaine v. villamil, senior science research specialist (srs), delivered a lecture on earthquake and earthquake hazards in ligao city. ms. fatima m. moncada, srs ii, shared a discussion on ashfall preparedness. ms. rygin joy r. matias, srs i, facilitated the earthquake preparedness guide while ms. jana marie dasalla, project technical aide vi, taught the participants on hazard maps appreciation. the hybrid activity equips participants with the practical knowledge and skills to anticipate, prepare for, and respond to various natural hazards, from identifying risks to performing drr measures as they continue to in line with 2025 handa pilipinas: para sa bagong pilipinas mindanao leg, dost ix and dost-phivolcs co-organized a session on #maghanda: communicating hazards, risk, and early warning for geologic hazards last september 25, 2025, at valencia hall, marcian garden hotel, zamboanga city. participants from lgus, the academe, and drr practitioners in the zamboanga peninsula joined the forum, which featured lectures on geologic hazards, tsunami preparedness, hazard maps, and phivolcs drr tools like georiskph and redas. dost-phivolcs director dr. teresito c. bacolcol reminded the participants that preparedness takes resources, but inaction costs far more, this event reinforces the call to use science-based tools and knowledge to protect lives and build resilient communities. tag: dost philippines dost regional office no. ix #handaangmayalam #onedost4u #solutionsopportunitiesforall #handapinas2025 #2025rstwinzampen in line with 2025 handa pilipinas: para sa bagong pilipinas mindanao leg, dost ix and dost-phivolcs co-organized a session on #maghanda: communicating hazards, risk, and early warning for geologic hazards last september 25, 2025, at valencia hall, marcian garden hotel, zamboanga city. participants from lgus, the academe, and drr practitioners in the zamboanga peninsula joined the forum, which featured lectures on geologic hazards, tsunami preparedness, hazard maps, and phivolcs drr tools like georiskph and redas. dost-phivolcs director dr. teresito c. bacolcol reminded the participants that preparedness takes resources, but inaction costs far more, this event reinforces the call to use science-based tools and knowledge to protect lives and build resilient communities. tag: dost philippines dost regional office no. ix #handaangmayalam #onedost4u #solutionsopportunitiesforall #handapinas2025 #2025rstwinzampen

press release: mmdrrmc preps for sts opong, regional inter-agency coordination cell activated according to pagasa issued tropical cyclone bulletin, at 5:00 pm today, opong maintains its strength while moving westward over the philippine sea. metro manila is still under tropical cyclone wind signal (tcws) no. 1 and is expecting possible significant rainfall from friday noon (26 september) until saturday morning (27 september). metro manila might reach tcws no. 2 or 3 at the most and overflow of nearby dams is not expected but not totally ruled out. considering the recent weather update, the metro manila disaster risk reduction and management council (mmdrrmc) convened for an emergency full council meeting attended by its member agencies and ncr local drrm offices to discuss preparedness measures for the possible impact of sts opong. the meeting was presided over by chairperson romando s. artes and mmda general manager usec procopio g. lipana, alongside senior-vice chairperson and ocd ncr regional director george f. keyser. the mmdrrmc emergency operations center (eoc) and response clusters are activated and was followed by a special meeting for the activation of the regional read: severe tropical storm (sts) opong caused massive destruction as it battered large parts of the visayas and bicol region, leaving at least four people dead and displacing more than 360,000 families, or about 1.414 million individuals, due to flooding and landslides. in its 11:00 p.m. bulletin, pagasa reported that sts opong was located 260 kilometers west of calapan city, oriental mindoro, as it moved over the west philippine sea. it is expected to exit the philippine area of responsibility (par) this morning or by midday, heading toward the northern part of vietnam with sustained winds of 110 kph and gusts of up to 135 kph. according to the office of civil defense (ocd), more than 87,000 residents in the bicol region evacuated, while around 73,000 individuals remain in evacuation centers in eastern samar and northern samar. in masbate, three fatalities were reported, including one crushed by a fallen tree, while another person in camarines norte was struck by lightning. around 20,000 people were affected in masbate, governor richard kho said. the storm impacted 11 regions, particularly 46 provinces, 391 cities and municipalities, and 2,891 barangays. experts have long warned that typhoons are becoming stronger and more frequent due to global warming, resulting in more severe damage to vulnerable communities. sts opong struck just days after super typhoon ragasa, which killed at least nine people and displaced thousands in northern luzon. the back-to-back disasters have made it more difficult for local governments to provide aid and repair damaged infrastructure. meanwhile, as the public struggles with the devastation brought by successive storms, a major controversy surrounds government flood control projects. investigations suggest that some officials may have profited from multi-billion peso kickbacks, allegedly spent on lavish lifestyles instead of urgently needed infrastructure against disasters. the issue sparked massive protests on september 21, 2025, at rizal park in manila and at the edsa people power monument in quezon city. the impact of sts opong goes beyond the loss of lives and properties, it also highlights the deeper issues the country faces, from the effects of climate change to corruption in projects that should have served as vital defenses against natural calamities. *the tagalog version can be read another student has developed a mapping website to help responders and donors locate earthquake-stricken communities in northern cebu. charles zoilo a. yana, 21, a 4th year computer engineering student from cebu technological university danao campus launched the northern cebu earthquake relief map guide on october 2, 2025, just two days after the magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the province. the platform allows users to pin exact locations and share key details, enabling volunteers and relief groups to coordinate assistance more effectively. yana explained that the tool works similarly to google maps, though not fully precise, as it relies on free online tools and available application programming interfaces. he added that project is entirely self-funded and not school-related, but was built purely out of his initiative to assist affected families. "we have two options to pin locations: one is to search the place there could be, suggest and recommend dropdowns or just simply enter and it will try to locate the location," yana explained. "second is manually, by clicking that green icon on the lower right corner, users can just zoom and navigate or find the nearest barangay," he added. since many affected residents in the north are offline and lack access to devices, yana said the platform depends entirely on crowdsourcing from people with relatives or information about those in need. | via sunstar cebu ctu danao campus facebook #allyouneedtoknow another student has developed a mapping website to help responders and donors locate earthquake-stricken communities in northern cebu. charles zoilo a. yana, 21, a 4th year computer engineering student from cebu technological university danao campus launched the northern cebu earthquake relief map guide on october 2, 2025, just two days after the magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the province. the platform allows users to pin exact locations and share key details, enabling volunteers and relief groups to coordinate assistance more effectively. yana explained that the tool works similarly to google maps, though not fully precise, as it relies on free online tools and available application programming interfaces. he added that project is entirely self-funded and not school-related, but was built purely out of his initiative to assist affected families. bogo bay fault: active fault na nag-generate ng m6.9 offshore northern cebu earthquake, tukoy na ng dost-phivolcs dost-phivolcs quick response team (qrt) found the onland extension of the newly-named bogo bay fault, which caused the magnitude 6.9 offshore northern cebu earthquake on september 30, 2025. located in sitio looc, brgy. nailon, bogo city, the team observed fault scarps, open cracks, and text_content: paano nga ba ako napadpad sa cebu kasama si boss ronald lewis ng kathy travel? oct.1 2025 at around 9pm tumawag si boss ronald at maam kathy saakin kung may mga appointment ba ako sabi ko wala po. suddenly sabi saakin ayusin mo na gamit mo at lilipad kayo ni boss ronald sa cebu! di na ako nagtanong kung anong reason basta alam ko ay may tumamang earthquake. maya-maya pa narecieved ko na ang ticket papunta dito sa cebu at dito na kami nagmeet ni boss ronald. habang nasa sasakyan kami nakakatuwa lang dahil walang bukang-bibig si boss ronald kundi we need to help some kababayan there. nakakatuwa talaga dahil walang post ang kathy travel about sa biglaang pagpunta dito sa cebu para tumulong at dun mo makikita na galing sa puso ang pagtulong na gagawin nila. at ito na nga ang nangyari nagpost ako kahapon na nandito kami sa cebu para tutulong sa ibang kababayan natin at nakatanggap ako ng ilang gustong magsend ng pera sa gcash ko pero tumanggi ako sa kadahilanang bago pa kami pumunta dito nakabili na sila boss ronald ng mga basic supply na ipapamigay at isa pa wala nang mabilhan ng mga ipapamigay pa. kaya para saan pa na tanggapin ko ang mga gustong magbigay ng tulong. kaya sa mga kababayan ko na nagmessage saakin na gustong tumulong ako at ang kathy travel hk limited ay nagpapasalamat sa inyo sa kagustuhan ninyong tumulong pero di po namin matatanggap yung mga gusto po ninyong ibigay dahil wala na rin po kaming makuhaan ng supply. at ito na nga po ito ay ilan lamang sa mga larawan na nabigyan namin ng tulong dahil sadyang naubusan na rin ng supply ang mga bigasan. maraming maraming salamat mga kababayan ko sa dasal at concern sa mga kababayan natin dito sa pilipinas. sa kathy travel hk limited di man ninyo pinapakita ang pagtulong ninyo pero ako ang saksi sa mga ginagawa ninyo. maraming salamat boss ronald lewis and maam cathrina lewis. #kathytravelhklimited #bryancalagui #fypviralfyp #fyp #cebuearthquake #earthquakealert paano nga ba ako napadpad sa cebu kasama si boss ronald lewis ng kathy travel? oct.1 2025 at around 9pm tumawag si boss ronald at maam kathy saakin kung may mga appointment ba ako sabi ko wala po. suddenly sabi saakin ayusin mo na gamit mo at lilipad kayo ni boss ronald sa cebu! hydrological situationer #30 for agno river issued at 9:00am, 04 october 2025 hydrological situationer #30 for agno river issued at 9:00am, 04 october 2025 paano mabubuo ang bagyo ay nabubuo sa ibabaw ng karagatan kung saan ang temperatura ng tubig ay mataas at mayroong kahalumigmigan sa hangin. narito ang mga hakbang sa pagbuo ng bagyo: pagsingaw ng tubig*: ang araw ay nagpapainit sa tubig ng karagatan, na nagreresulta sa pagsingaw ng tubig patungo sa atmospera. *pagtaas ng hangin*: ang mainit na hangin na mayroong kahalumigmigan ay tumataas patungo sa mataas na altitude. *pagkondensa ng ulap*: sa pagtaas ng hangin, ito ay lumalamig at nagiging sanhi ng pagkondensa ng singaw ng tubig sa anyo ng mga ulap. *pagbuo ng low-pressure area*: ang pagtaas ng hangin at pagkondensa ng ulap ay lumilikha ng isang lugar na may mababang presyon sa ibabaw ng karagatan. *pag-ikot ng hangin*: ang hangin mula sa paligid ay dumadaloy patungo sa gitna ng low-pressure area, na nagiging sanhi ng pag-ikot ng hangin dahil sa epekto ng coriolis. *paglakas ng bagyo*: kung ang mga kondisyon ay angkop (sapat na init ng tubig at kahalumigmigan), ang sistema ay patuloy na lumalakas at nagiging isang bagyo. *pag-uuri ng bagyo*: depende sa lakas ng hangin at organisasyon ng sistema, ito ay maaaring uriin bilang tropical depression, tropical storm, o typhoon kung ito ay lumakas pa. ang mga bagyo ay karaniwang nabubuo sa mga rehiyon na malapit sa ekwador, kung saan ang temperatura ng tubig ay sapat na mainit upang suportahan ang pagbuo ng mga bagyo.

text_content: ocd chief cabreros leads mission in disaster-stricken masbate, cebu civil defense administrator, undersecretary harold cabreros was on a week-long mission to assess the impact of calamitiestropical cyclone opong in masbate and the magnitude 6.9 earthquake in cebu. usec. cabreros was in masbate earlier this week to assess the aftermath of tropical cyclone opong and join a briefing with president ferdinand marcos jr. when the strong earthquake struck cebu on tuesday evening. it is deeply saddening to witness the struggles faced by our fellow filipinos due to the geohazards assessment across several areas in cebu province. the assessment aims to identify zones susceptible to flooding, rain-induced landslides, ground subsidence, and sinkhole formation. the liquefaction is a phenomenon where a solid or a gas transforms into a liquid state. let's explore it in different contexts relevant to the philippines. *what is liquefaction?* liquefaction occurs when a solid material, often soil or sand saturated with water, loses its strength and stiffness due to increased pore water pressure, typically caused by seismic shaking during earthquakes. this leads the solid to behave like a liquid. *causes of liquefaction* 1. *earthquakes*: ground shaking can cause water-saturated granular soils (like sand) to lose strength. 2. *water saturation*: soils that are fully saturated with water are more prone to liquefaction. 3. *soil composition*: loose, granular soils are more susceptible. *effects of liquefaction* - *structural damage*: buildings and infrastructure can suffer significant damage or collapse. - *ground settlement*: areas can experience uneven settling. - *lateral spreading*: ground can move laterally, damaging structures. *liquefaction in the philippines* the philippines is seismically active, located in the pacific ring of fire, making it vulnerable to earthquakes and associated hazards like liquefaction. areas with soft, water-saturated soils are at higher risk. *notable examples* - *1990 luzon earthquake*: caused significant damage, illustrating the country's vulnerability to seismic hazards. - *areas at risk*: regions like metro manila, parts of luzon, and other seismically active zones could be susceptible depending on soil conditions. *mitigation and considerations* - *geotechnical investigations*: assessing soil conditions is crucial for construction in prone areas. - *engineering designs*: structures can be designed to mitigate liquefaction risks. - *land use planning*: awareness and planning can help reduce risks. *other contexts* liquefaction can also refer to processes in industries (like lng - liquefied natural gas) or natural processes like mudflows, but earthquake-induced soil liquefaction is often a key concern in seismic zones like the philippines. is there a specific aspect of liquefaction you're interested in, like its impact on construction, earthquake preparedness, or something else?

text_content: disaster response update | boc extends aid to earthquake-hit families in cebu to help the victims of the recent earthquake in cebu, the bureau of customs (boc) turned over abandoned and forfeited goods to the office of civil defense (ocd). the donation, which came mostly from the manila international container port (micp), includes 56 pieces of rapid emergency tents and 1,087 pieces of assorted tents to serve as temporary shelters, 50 units of mobile power supply to provide electricity in affected areas, and one bio-toilet unit to ensure proper sanitation for displaced residents. the donated items were declared abandoned and subsequently forfeited in favor of the government. in line with customs procedures and upon approval, these goods were officially released and turned over to the office of civil defense (ocd) to support its ongoing relief and recovery efforts. aside from the forfeited items, boc officials and personnel also donated over 100 sacks of rice to support food assistance efforts. boc commissioner ariel f. nepomuceno, who previously served as undersecretary of the department of national defense and administrator of the ocd, emphasized the significance of ensuring that government resources are directed to the people in times of crisis. in moments like this, every donation can make a difference for our countrymen who have lost their homes and security. having worked with the ocd in the past, alam ko po firsthand kung gaano kahalaga na mabilis, maayos, at diretso ang tulong sa mga kababayan nating nasalanta," said commissioner nepomuceno. micp district collector rizalino jose c. torralba expressed his full support for the initiative, reaffirming the ports commitment to utilizing abandoned and forfeited goods for the benefit of the public. the manila international container port stands in full support of the bocs thrust to transform abandoned goods into opportunities for service. through this donation, we hope to extend help and bring comfort to our fellow filipinos in cebu who are recovering from this calamity, said collector torralba. the ocd will handle the distribution of the donated items to affected families in cebu, ensuring that they reach communities most in need. this partnership highlights the coordination of government agencies to maximize resources and deliver timely support during emergencies. source: bureau of cebus fault line: what you need to know cebu is not just a busy and modern city, it also sits on top of the central cebu fault system, a major fault line that can generate strong earthquakes. this fault runs through danao, compostela, cebu city, talisay, minglanilla, naga, balamban, and toledo. it has four main faults: balamban, central highland, uling-masaba, and lutac-jaclupan. the longest, the uling-masaba fault, can produce a magnitude 7.1 quake, as strong as the 2013 bohol earthquake. cebu has already felt strong earthquakes before, including the 2012 negros quake, the 2013 bohol quake, and the 2025 cebu quake. these remind us that the risk is real. this isnt to cause fear, but to raise awareness. earthquakes cannot be prevented, but being prepared, through stronger buildings, disaster drills, and emergency kits, can save lives. stay informed. stay prepared. #earthquakealert #earthquakepreparedness #cebu #cebunibai cebus fault line: what you need to know cebu is not just a busy and modern city, it also sits on top of the central cebu fault system, a major fault line that can generate strong earthquakes. this fault runs through danao, compostela, cebu city, talisay, minglanilla, naga, balamban, and toledo. it has four main faults: balamban, central highland, uling-masaba, and lutac-jaclupan. the longest, the uling-masaba fault, can produce a magnitude 7.1 quake, as strong as the 2013 bohol earthquake. cebu has already felt strong earthquakes before, including the 2012 negros quake, the 2013 bohol quake, and the 2025 cebu quake. these remind us that the risk is real. this isnt to cause fear, but to raise awareness. earthquakes cannot be prevented, but being prepared, through stronger buildings, disaster drills, and emergency kits, can save lives. stay informed. stay prepared. #earthquakealert #earthquakepreparedness #cebu #cebunibai

climate campaigners led by the asian peoples movement on debt and development (apmdd) hold a protest outside a hotel in pasay city on tuesday, october 7, 2025, as the fund for responding to loss and damage (frld) board meets. in the philippines and throughout asia, climate disasters have resulted in massive losses of livelihoods, infrastructure, crops, and even lives. both economic and non-economic losses are increasing dramatically with each passing year, but governments of the global north are not meeting their responsibility to mobilize adequate resources, said climate activist and apmdd coordinator lidy nacpil. they are extremely reluctant to provide the funds they owe to the south. climate impacts are estimated to cost at least $894 billion annually by 2030, a conservative figure that doesnt account for lost lives, cultures, and ecosystems. in truth, rich countries should be paying a total of at least $1 trillion per year to the frld. yet governments have delivered only $360 million, which is nowhere near enough," she added. the group called on global north governments to increase funding for climate loss and damage and to stop financing what they described as the city, october 7, 2025 the arrival of brp dagupan city (ls551) at maya port, daanbantayan on october 6, 2025 marked a significant boost in the ongoing relief and rehabilitation efforts in northern cebu. the pn ship delivered essential relief supplies and heavy equipment to support communities severely affected by the recent earthquake, underscoring the philippine navys vital role in accelerating recovery operations in the visayas region. ls551 brought a substantial shipment of relief aid, food packs, clean drinking water, hygiene kits, medical supplies and temporary shelters, providing essential support to communities struggling in the wake of the disaster. beyond basic necessities, the pn ship also carried vital support equipment to enhance on-ground coordination. among its cargoes were the vehicles from valenzuela disaster risk reduction and management office (vdrrmo) as well as the communications van from naval cyber warfare force (ncwf). relatedly, said communications van will serve as a platform to provide mobile, reliable and secure communication support to naval and joint operations especially to the two (2) pn disaster response and rescue teams (drrt) of this command that were deployed to joint task force handa under the visayas command to address the concern of some areas in northern cebu where fixed communication infrastructure is unavailable, damaged or disrupted. commo joselito e de guzman pn, commander, naval forces central (cnfc) personally supervised the overall conduct of humanitarian assistance and disaster response (hadr) operations carried out by team nfc in northern cebu, particularly in the municipalities of daanbantayan, bantayan island, and medellin. his leadership ensured the synchronized execution of relief distribution, logistics coordination and inter-agency collaboration with the office of civil defense 7 (ocd7), department of social welfare and development 7 (dswd7) and concerned local government units (lgu). through his direct supervision, the command was able to maximize the efficiency of maritime and land-based operations, guarantee the timely delivery of essential aid, and uphold the navys commitment in serving communities affected by the recent calamity. following the relief mission in daanbantayan, ls551 proceeded to cebu via capt veloso pier, nbrr to offload remaining essential supplies in support to ongoing hadr operations. the ship will then accommodate new load of relief goods and rehabilitation materials bound for the hardest-hit areas in northern cebu, further bolstering relief, recovery and rebuilding efforts. while currently docked in cebu, ls551 remains on standby and ready to accommodate both rolling and loose cargos intended for continued relief and rehabilitation efforts in the affected northern cebu communities. naval forces central, your navy in the visayas remains steadfast in its commitment in delivering swift and efficient disaster response. with the continued deployment of assets like ls551, nfc ensures timely support for both relief and rehabilitation efforts, working hand-in-hand with local and national agencies to president ferdinand r. marcos jr., together with labor secretary bienvenido laguesma and tesda director general secretary kiko benitez, visited the training facilities inside the technical education and skills development authority (tesda) compound in taguig city on friday, october 10. the president inspected workshops and equipment for welding, mechatronics, visual graphics, and more, and witnessed how tesda integrates hands-on learning with industry collaboration. to recall, during his fourth state of the nation address (sona) in july, marcos underscored the growing importance of technical-vocational education and training (tvet) in providing employment and access to higher learning. tech-voc, he said, has been proven effective and is gradually being incorporated into the senior high school curriculum. text_content: ocd chief leads assessment in davao after "doublet earthquake" october 12, 2025 office of civil defense (ocd) administrator, undersecretary harold cabreros, led an aerial and ground assessment in the davao region on saturday following the "doublet earthquake"two main shocks that struck davao oriental on friday morning and evening. usec. cabreros arrived in davao city late friday evening and immediately met with ocd davao regional director ednar dayanghirang and operations center staff to discuss the situation. follow-up briefings were conducted on saturday morning with the ocd davao region and the tactical operations group davao to finalize plans for the aerial survey and ocular inspections. the assessment team included representatives from the mines and geosciences bureau (mgb), the philippine institute of volcanology and seismology (phivolcs), ocd davao director dayanghirang, and officers from uniformed services. aside from aerial survey, their activities included a meeting with davao oriental governor nelson dayanghirang in mati; inspection of several damaged facilities in manay, davao oriental, including a community hospital and a barangay hall; and a coordination meeting in pantukan, davao de oro, with governor raul mabanglo and local officials to address landslides and ongoing threats in the municipality. following the assessment, usec. cabreros reported online to an inter-agency meeting of ndrrmc, confirming the priority areas based on the severity of damage in davao: manay, davao oriental tarragona, davao oriental mati city, davao oriental pantukan, davao de oro we did an air survey of affected areas and ocular inspections of the ground. we have validated initial damages, based on our collaboration with lgus and governors of davao de oro, davao oriental, the mayor of manay, and the mayor of pantukan. manay is the priority, then tarragona, mati, and finally pantukan, in that order. he stated. usec. cabreros highlighted the vulnerability of health infrastructure, noting that the health sector was the "most affected." the davao oriental provincial hospital in manay is currently non-operational due to heavy and structurally unstable damage. concerned agencies are coordinating structural and functional assessments of all damaged health facilities to prioritize repair needs and identify safe alternative patient accommodation to ensure operational continuity. phivolcs recorded two main tremors in manay, davao oriental, on friday: a magnitude 7.4 earthquake at 9:43 a.m., followed by a magnitude 6.8 shock at 7:12 p.m. tsunami warnings were issued, prompting forced evacuations led by local disaster risk reduction and management (drrm) offices, the philippine national police (pnp), the philippine coast guard (pcg), and the department of tourism (dot). these warnings were subsequently lifted. the highest reported intensity in manay was intensity vi. basic needs, including food and water, are reported as sufficient in affected areas, with temporary shelters provided by respective local government units. the national government has assured its readiness to augment resources as needed. ocd davao region and other affected regions are continuously conducting assessments and coordinating with local drrm councils. various government agencies and uniformed services have been holding a series of coordination meetings since friday to monitor the situation and coordinate assistance on the ground. #civildefenseph #protectingthepeople #servingthenation #ligtasangbayankunghandaangmamamayan [ rd in action ] day 2 | rd conducts site assessment and monitoring in quake-hit areas of davao oriental earlier today, fcsupt junito f maslang, regional director of the bureau of fire protection region 11, together with fsupt joycelyn hernaez-grant, provincial fire marshal, fcinsp paul jorge c barrozo, and fsinsp elizabeth d capina, personally visited the municipalities of manay and tarragona in davao oriental to assess the impact of the magnitude 7.6 earthquake that recently struck the province. the team conducted thorough inspection and monitoring activities at critical areas, including manay fire station, davao oriental provincial hospital, tarragona municipal hall, and tarragona fire station, to evaluate structural integrity and ensure operational readiness of bfp units. during the visit, fcsupt maslang met with key officials of both municipalities to coordinate efforts and reinforce the bureaus support in the ongoing response and recovery operations. he emphasized the importance of close collaboration between the bfp and the local government units (lgus) to ensure the safety of affected residents and the swift restoration of essential services. the regional director likewise commended the dedication of bfp personnel on the ground, urging them to remain vigilant and proactive in assisting local authorities in disaster response and community safety operations. dagat. ang ganitong pagguho ay puwedeng maglatag ng dagdag na gibain sa pagtaas o pagbaba ng tubig sa baybayin. itoy mas subtle at mahirap mapansin agad. aftershocks / chain reaction dahil datiy nagkaroon ng malalakas na lindol sa ibat ibang bahagi ng pilipinas nitong mga nakaraang araw (halimbawa sa cebu) , may posibilidad na ang stress sa mga fault lines ay nagaccumulate. kapag may lindol text_content: tropical storm ramil makes landfall in sorsogon; heavy rains threaten luzon and visayas tropical storm ramil (international name: fengshen) has officially made landfall in southeastern luzon, near sorsogon and the bicol region, after tracking slightly farther south and west than early forecasts predicted. now moving slowly westward, ramil is expected to cross the bicol region before heading toward southern and central luzon, including areas near metro manila and pangasinan, throughout the weekend. pagasa has raised signal no. 2 over parts of northern samar and the eastern coast. however, the main concern is heavy rainfall, not wind with 100 to 200 mm expected along the east coast and 50 to 150 mm across bicol, samar, and eventually much of luzon. residents are warned of localized flooding and landslides, especially in mountainous and low-lying areas. even regions north of the storms center may experience widespread rain due to its broad convection. authorities urge the public to stay alert and not focus solely on the storms center track, as outer rainbands often cause the most significant impacts. #ramilph #fengshen #pagasa #bicolregion #sorsogon #luzon #visayas #weatherupdate #floodalert #landslidewarning #bagyongramil #turismocentralluzon tropical storm ramil makes landfall in sorsogon;
